::: {.front card-id="study-identity" tags="definition"}
State the identity law in a group $G$.
:::

::: {.back card-id="study-identity"}
There is $e\in G$ such that $eg=ge=g$ for every $g\in G$.
:::

::: {.front card-id="study-inverse" tags="definition"}
State the inverse law in a group $G$ with identity $e$.
:::

::: {.back card-id="study-inverse"}
For each $g\in G$ there is $g^{-1}\in G$ with $gg^{-1}=g^{-1}g=e$.
:::

::: {.front card-id="study-abelian" tags="definition"}
When is a group $G$ abelian?
:::

::: {.back card-id="study-abelian"}
$gh=hg$ for all $g,h\in G$.
:::

::: {.front card-id="study-associative" tags="definition"}
State associativity of the group operation on $G$.
:::

::: {.back card-id="study-associative"}
$(gh)k=g(hk)$ for all $g,h,k\in G$.
:::
